name: Philip the Evangelist
bio: Philip was one of seven men chosen by the disciples to oversee the daily distribution of food to free the apostles for prayer and teaching; the apostles prayed and laid hands on him and the other six (Acts 6:1-6). He is a different figure from Philip the apostle. His further role as an evangelist is told in detail in the chapters ahead. When persecution scattered believers from Jerusalem, Philip went to Samaria and preached Christ there, performing miracles and casting out unclean spirits to great joy in the city; among his converts was Simon the sorcerer. An angel then directed Philip to the desert road to Gaza, where he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of Queen Candace, reading Isaiah in his chariot; Philip explained that the prophet's suffering servant was Jesus, and when the eunuch asked to be baptized, Philip baptized him on the spot before being miraculously carried away. Philip then preached throughout the region until reaching Caesarea (Acts 8:5-40).
